correctness.rationale: For all n>=1 the first selected center arc A_i or B_i has respectively C_i or D_i as a compatible toggle. Every face outside the outer cross-polytope complex is paired exactly once. In the directed Hasse graph the center arc set never increases; after it stabilizes, every nonpivot outer arc can only be deleted and the pivot outer arc can only be added. This proves acyclicity and hence an elementary collapse onto a join of n zero-spheres. The join orientation cycle establishes the integral S_n by C_2 sign character. The predicted face polynomial counts 0, 1, or 2 center arcs exhaustively. Standalone code independently enumerates 1<=n<=7, all faces/381024 Hasse covers at n=7, and signed orientation actions.

value.rationale: A fully bidirected length-two spider is the first uniform genuinely branching single-hub tree family beyond previously published paths and polygonal digraphs. The theorem gives a natural all-parameter integral simple-homotopy collapse to a cross-polytope sphere, a complete integral arm-permutation/reversal character, and an exact full face enumerator. This exposes structural vanishing of extra face dimensions and a symmetry parity law, not a routine small-parameter table; no generic-tree classification is claimed.
